_doc: Register of fuzz findings that are known, reproduced, and awaiting a product decision (#839 G10). Keyed by the invariant class in scripts/fuzz/targets.mjs. A finding whose class is listed here is reported by `bun run test:fuzz` without failing the lane, because scripts/fuzz/replay.test.mjs pins its exact current behaviour: the day the product changes, that suite goes red and the entry must be revisited. A finding whose class is NOT listed fails the lane. Removing an entry is how a fix gets locked in — never add one to go green.

wal.closer-roundtrip-rejected.note: packages/backup/src/wal-format.ts: CLOSER_KEY_RE (:252) admits `closed-000000000000`, but assertValidCloser (:306) requires endOffset > 0 — so parseWalCloserKey returns a WalGroupCloser that walGroupCloserKey then refuses to re-emit. The two halves of the codec disagree about what a legal closer is. A provider listing carrying that key is read as a closed group at offset 0 by wal-restore.ts:145 and backup-reconciliation.ts:133. Product fix (add the `\d{12}` positivity check to the parser, or relax the formatter) is out of scope for the harness slice that found it.

fts-mirror.decision.note: packages/client/src/replica/search.ts:49 documents itself as mirroring the canonical gateway, but its token regex admits \p{M} (combining marks) while packages/vault/src/gateway/search.ts:35 requires \p{L} or \p{N}. A query of only combining marks is refused online and searched offline — the replica answers a question the gateway declines.

fts-mirror.expression.note: Same mirror claim, different half: the gateway splits on whitespace only, so `don't` compiles to one prefix phrase, while the replica re-splits on Unicode word runs and compiles two. The 16-token bound is therefore applied to different token streams, so the two planes rank and truncate differently for any query containing punctuation.
